Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

Relocation assistance available

Most schools have someone whose job is keeping parents happy. Alpha needs someone parents trust. That is a different job and a harder one: you will tell these families no, and they will think more of you for it.

You'll be the person families call when something feels off, when they're uncertain, or when they want to share a moment they know you'll understand. You'll know each family well enough to anticipate what they need before they ask. You'll also be the person who says no when the answer is no: clearly, with the reasoning, without flinching. Roles that trade hard conversations for short-term satisfaction build polite, fragile communities. This one builds committed ones.

You won't do it alone, and you won't do it around the Guides who mentor these students. You are the parent-facing side of a leadership partnership with your Guides: aligned with them before and after every sensitive conversation, protective of their authority with students, and willing to take family issues off their plate so they can coach. Ambiguous situations land on you. A student incident, a conflict between families, a decision you have to make on the spot with incomplete information. You decide, and you own the outcome.

What you own beyond that depends on where your campus is in its life. At a launch or under-enrolled campus, you own school growth. At a mature campus with dedicated admissions staff, you concentrate on retention, referrals, and the depth of the community. Same role, different center of gravity, and it can shift as the campus matures.

Alpha isn't a traditional school. Students finish core academics in two hours a day using AI-powered apps, then spend the rest of their time on public speaking, critical thinking, and real-world projects. No lectures. No busywork. Top 1% results nationwide. The families who choose it are paying for something they believe in, and belief needs tending. You'll carry that conversation with every family, through every doubt, for as long as their child is enrolled.

If defending an unconventional model to sophisticated skeptics sounds like a burden, this role isn't for you. If it sounds like the most interesting conversation you could be having, keep reading.

Own the relationship with every family on campus, and lead the hard conversations. Find the real concern, deliver a clear decision, hold it, and follow through until it stays resolved. This is also where you defend Alpha's model through screen-time worries, skeptical relatives, and moments of doubt.
Operate as the parent-facing co-leader alongside your Guides. Align before and after sensitive conversations, protect the coaching relationship they hold with students, take family issues off their plate, and make sure families always know who owns what.
Make the real-time calls in ambiguous student and family situations, and route child-safety, legal, and high-risk matters through the correct escalation path immediately. Telling those two apart on the spot is the judgment this job turns on.
Build the community: campus traditions, parent networks, and local partnerships, each with a defined outcome behind it, plus the trusted parent champions who become the campus's most credible voice.
Own the growth contribution your campus phase calls for, against outcomes agreed up front and tracked as the campus changes. At a launch or under-enrolled campus, that means developing local demand and personally owning admissions follow-through to enrollment. At a mature campus it means retention, referrals, and clean handoffs to admissions.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Passing concerns along to someone else. You are a decision-maker, not a liaison, and "I'll raise it with the team" is not an answer families should hear from you.
Keeping the peace by saying yes, softening a standard, bending the model, or treating parent concerns as a ticket queue rather than as relationships that need boundaries.
Escalating every ambiguous situation to avoid owning the call, or at the other extreme, sitting on something that genuinely belongs with campus leadership, safety, or legal.
Taking over the mentoring and coaching decisions that belong to your Guides, or leaving Guides to absorb parent issues you should have resolved.
Routine school administration, desk work, or waiting for a playbook, an established process, or a full team before you act.

Legally authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship
5+ years personally owning high-trust relationships with families, clients, donors, or members, where your judgment and follow-through changed retention or advocacy
A track record of holding firm decisions with demanding stakeholders without losing the relationship
Independent ownership of an ambiguous relationship, community, or growth outcome, with results you can point to as your own
Willing to own school growth and admissions follow-through when your campus phase calls for it
Clear, concise communication that earns confidence quickly with affluent, high-expectation families
Familiarity with independent, private, or non-traditional education
Hands-on daily use of AI tools, and genuine conviction about AI-powered education

"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

The families who choose Alpha rarely arrive from an ad. They arrive because another family sat across from them at dinner and said, "This changed my kid." That word-of-mouth engine is the thing you would own for an entire region: the dinners, the parent ambassadors, the mayor's office, the CEO who opens a door for a 14-year-old's first real project.

A normal week puts you in four rooms. You design and host the region's calendar of gatherings, from a 150-person open house to an eight-seat curated dinner, several a month. You recruit current parents who genuinely want to talk to prospective ones and match them, family to family. You build relationships with city officials and business leaders, turning them into venues, sources of support for new campus openings, and real opportunities for students. And you deliver on the Alpha Networks: introductions, expert masterclasses, internships, alumni welcomes, logged family by family.

There is no finished playbook. You write it while running it, and the systems you invent get picked up by peers building the same engine in other cities. As the region grows, the scoreboard gets harder, not easier: doors opened per family has to rise even as enrollment climbs. Success shows up as the share of growth arriving through real people vouching for Alpha, read on a multi-year trend rather than a quarterly report.

No degree is required, and no particular pedigree. An MBA, a consulting or wealth-management career, and a self-made run in community, hospitality, or advancement all count the same here. What we read is the track record of convening people and turning those relationships into value.

This role is on-site in one of the following regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. Expect evenings and weekends in rooms full of high-expectation parents, elected officials, and founders, plus regular local travel. You will be the most connected person in your city, and you will spend that on kids. If that trade sounds like the point rather than the cost, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Designing and running the region's gathering calendar: open events, curated dinners by city and grade, and family retreats, several a month and on budget
Securing venues, hosts, and vendors, then hosting the room live
Recruiting current parents as ambassadors, equipping them with true stories, and matching them to prospective families and tours
Opening relationships with public officials and business executives, and turning them into venues, campus-opening support, and student opportunities
Matching enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, masterclasses, and real-world internships, and welcoming graduating families as alumni within 30 days
Logging every gathering, introduction, and first-contact attribution in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) so "doors opened per family" is a true number

What You Won’t Be Doing

Buying growth — this role has no paid media, no ad spend, and no impression or lead-volume targets
Owning the brand story or top-down campaigns; Marketing has that
Processing admissions, running tours, or chasing enrollment paperwork; Admissions and Family Success have that
Running a campus day-to-day, or opening the physical building
Reporting raw attendance and headcount as if a full room were the result
Waiting for a finished playbook, a template, or support staff before you start

Director Of Advancement Key Responsibilities

Make people-first referrals the majority source of your region's enrollment growth.

Basic Requirements

5+ years building communities or relationship programs in K-12 education, membership, or a comparable network business, where growth came through people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client book, with numbers to show for it
Has personally designed and run 20+ gatherings across the full range, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ person open events, with budget ownership
Has opened and maintained relationships with public officials or business executives that produced concrete, nameable value
Disciplined CRM user; logging relationships, attributions, and actions is already a habit
Lives in, or will relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Authorized to work in the US without visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Ran regional growth, community, or partnerships for a network-shaped organization: a school group, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic institution
Built and monetized a high-trust book of relationships as a client-facing principal in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Came up through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and were always the one asked to host and represent the institution
Existing relationships with local government or the business community in your city
Fluent in how families make high-stakes education decisions

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

new_jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
"Alpha School students, on average, experience 2.4 to 2.6 times the academic growth of traditional school students"

— Forbes

Alpha is hiring.

On-site (multiple cities - see Requirements)
W2 Employee
$200K/yr, with Park City at $250K/yr
Relocation assistance available

Most schools have someone whose job is keeping parents happy. Alpha needs someone parents trust. That is a different job and a harder one: you will tell these families no, and they will think more of you for it.

You'll be the person families call when something feels off, when they're uncertain, or when they want to share a moment they know you'll understand. You'll know each family well enough to anticipate what they need before they ask. You'll also be the person who says no when the answer is no: clearly, with the reasoning, without flinching. Roles that trade hard conversations for short-term satisfaction build polite, fragile communities. This one builds committed ones.

You won't do it alone, and you won't do it around the Guides who mentor these students. You are the parent-facing side of a leadership partnership with your Guides: aligned with them before and after every sensitive conversation, protective of their authority with students, and willing to take family issues off their plate so they can coach. Ambiguous situations land on you. A student incident, a conflict between families, a decision you have to make on the spot with incomplete information. You decide, and you own the outcome.

What you own beyond that depends on where your campus is in its life. At a launch or under-enrolled campus, you own school growth. At a mature campus with dedicated admissions staff, you concentrate on retention, referrals, and the depth of the community. Same role, different center of gravity, and it can shift as the campus matures.

Alpha isn't a traditional school. Students finish core academics in two hours a day using AI-powered apps, then spend the rest of their time on public speaking, critical thinking, and real-world projects. No lectures. No busywork. Top 1% results nationwide. The families who choose it are paying for something they believe in, and belief needs tending. You'll carry that conversation with every family, through every doubt, for as long as their child is enrolled.

If defending an unconventional model to sophisticated skeptics sounds like a burden, this role isn't for you. If it sounds like the most interesting conversation you could be having, keep reading.

What You Will Be Doing

Own the relationship with every family on campus, and lead the hard conversations. Find the real concern, deliver a clear decision, hold it, and follow through until it stays resolved. This is also where you defend Alpha's model through screen-time worries, skeptical relatives, and moments of doubt.
Operate as the parent-facing co-leader alongside your Guides. Align before and after sensitive conversations, protect the coaching relationship they hold with students, take family issues off their plate, and make sure families always know who owns what.
Make the real-time calls in ambiguous student and family situations, and route child-safety, legal, and high-risk matters through the correct escalation path immediately. Telling those two apart on the spot is the judgment this job turns on.
Build the community: campus traditions, parent networks, and local partnerships, each with a defined outcome behind it, plus the trusted parent champions who become the campus's most credible voice.
Own the growth contribution your campus phase calls for, against outcomes agreed up front and tracked as the campus changes. At a launch or under-enrolled campus, that means developing local demand and personally owning admissions follow-through to enrollment. At a mature campus it means retention, referrals, and clean handoffs to admissions.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Passing concerns along to someone else. You are a decision-maker, not a liaison, and "I'll raise it with the team" is not an answer families should hear from you.
Keeping the peace by saying yes, softening a standard, bending the model, or treating parent concerns as a ticket queue rather than as relationships that need boundaries.
Escalating every ambiguous situation to avoid owning the call, or at the other extreme, sitting on something that genuinely belongs with campus leadership, safety, or legal.
Taking over the mentoring and coaching decisions that belong to your Guides, or leaving Guides to absorb parent issues you should have resolved.
Routine school administration, desk work, or waiting for a playbook, an established process, or a full team before you act.

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

The job comes down to four ownership areas: the trust, retention, and advocacy of every current family; the parent-facing partnership with your Guides and the real-time judgment calls that come with it; the campus's community life; and the growth contribution your campus's phase requires. Build a campus where families stay, Guides feel backed, and hard decisions get made quickly and credibly.

Basic Requirements

Live within commuting distance of one of these campuses, or relocate within 60 days: Boca Raton, FL; Burlington, VT; Jackson Hole, WY; Lake Travis, TX; Las Vegas, NV; Palm Beach, FL; Park City, UT; Tulsa, OK
Compensation is $200,000 per year for the listed campuses, except Park City, which is $250,000 per year
On-site full-time, including early mornings, late afternoons, evening events 2–3x/month, and occasional weekends
Legally authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship
5+ years personally owning high-trust relationships with families, clients, donors, or members, where your judgment and follow-through changed retention or advocacy
A track record of holding firm decisions with demanding stakeholders without losing the relationship
Independent ownership of an ambiguous relationship, community, or growth outcome, with results you can point to as your own
Willing to own school growth and admissions follow-through when your campus phase calls for it
Clear, concise communication that earns confidence quickly with affluent, high-expectation families
Familiarity with independent, private, or non-traditional education
Hands-on daily use of AI tools, and genuine conviction about AI-powered education

Benefits and other compensation: Health coverage (medical, dental, vision), life and disability insurance, voluntary benefits, tax-advantaged FSA, HSA, and commuter accounts, and a 401(k). Paid time off and parental leave. A one-time relocation allowance.

Nice-to-have Requirements

Exceptional candidates will have at least one of the following:

An established local network in the campus city, whether school, civic, faith, business, or community, that you can activate quickly
Private or independent school experience with a track record of family retention and community depth, not just enrollment numbers
Experience as the relationship owner alongside educators or other professionals, where you held the family, and they held the craft, and neither of you undermined the other
A launch or early-stage assignment where you personally built local demand and saw it through to committed families
An instinct for creating experiences (events, moments, environments) where people feel they belong to something worth protecting
Startup or early-stage experience where you built from nothing and stayed grounded when things changed quickly
